# Sakuragaoka reference and design record

Date inspected: 2026-10-07. These two game buildings are original architectural syntheses, not surveyed reconstructions. All dimensions are author-selected estimates in metres. Real building names are used here only to identify the references; the GLBs have the fictional signs HANA and KOHANA WORKS.

## Actual photographs inspected

### Residential balcony character: Park Axis Shibuya Sakuragaoka West

- Publisher: Ken Corporation property listing, https://www.kencorp.com/rent/yokohamaapartment/search/results/151467.html
- Image inspected at full downloaded 1024 × 683 pixels: https://www.kencorp.com/assets/image/building/151467/151467_q1.jpg
- Visible evidence: long stacked recessed balconies; darker lower privacy bands and lighter/frosted upper balcony panels; thin metal rails and dividing walls; a narrow pale vertical end pier; several air-conditioner condensers inside balcony recesses; landscaped, set-back ground approach.
- Location confidence: named listing identifies Park Axis Shibuya Sakuragaoka West. This is a 14-storey reference, not the model's seven-storey height. The model intentionally changes floor count, footprint, entry, materials arrangement and roof profile.
- Usage: visual study only. Photo carries Ken Corporation watermark. No open redistribution or texture-reuse permission was established. No photo pixels, crop, or derivative texture are included in the assets or repository.

### Residential low/midrise proportion and rail detail: Sakuragaoka Urban Life B

- Publisher: Tokyu Livable, https://www.livable.co.jp/mansion/library/000000015909/
- Exterior image actually inspected at 1000 × 751 pixels: https://www.livable.co.jp/project-image/15/159/15909/15909_22553380.jpg?20180410182655
- Visible evidence: pale concrete slabs; deep usable balconies; thin rails over low solid balcony upstands; apartment separator panels; sliding doors; condensers and exposed drainage at one end; darker ground-floor entrance/shop plane.
- Location confidence: page explicitly identifies Sakuragaoka Urban Life B in Shibuya's Sakuragaokacho. The page says four above-ground storeys for B; other whole-complex sources may give five. The model uses neither number as a surveyed fact and combines these midrise details with West's material contrast.
- Usage: visual study only. No image redistribution permission established; photo not included and never used as a texture.

### Office massing and common entry: Ninomiya Building

- Publisher: billage official tenant/location page, https://svdev.billage.space/shibuya/ninomiya
- Exterior actually inspected at 523 × 393 pixels: https://svdev.billage.space/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/010_shibuya_ninomiya_slider.jpg
- Entry actually inspected at 523 × 393 pixels: https://svdev.billage.space/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/009_shibuya_ninomiya_slider.jpg
- The page identifies the location as Ninomiya Building, 18-4 Sakuragaokacho, Shibuya, Tokyo.
- Exterior evidence: a compact white/tiled office mass; continuous dark ribbon windows; angled/chamfered corner geometry; long solid spandrel bands; small hedge border; varied setbacks. Entry evidence: glazed double-height-looking frontage at human scale, warm timber framing and shared workspace behind a recessed threshold. The model does not reproduce the tenant's logo or furniture.
- Interpretation: KOHANA WORKS has five above-ground office storeys with 3.2 m typical floor height, an invented communal terrace, and invented roof equipment. These features express the local office type while deliberately avoiding an exact copy or an unsupported claim about the real building's upper plan.
- Usage: visual study only. Published photos have no identified open image reuse license. No photographs are bundled or baked into textures.

## Additional context, not used as texture

Architecture reference worker supplied this verified Commons record: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Construction_seen_from_Shibuya_Stream_2.jpg . Creator Syced, CC0 1.0. Elevated view from Shibuya Stream toward Sakuragaoka, depicting Park Axis South and West in context. This record can be used by integrators for contextual comparison, but this worker's direct visual decisions came from the three exterior photographs and one entry photograph listed above.

## What is known vs invented

- Verified visually: balcony depth and individual separation; contrast between apartment openings and office ribbon glazing; set-back/common ground-floor treatment; thin rails, condensed services and planter placement as local architectural cues.
- Invented estimates: all model dimensions, exact seven/five storey configurations, roof service layouts, rear/side window rhythm, terrace layout, courtyard depth, unit count and sign placement.
- The photos are perspective images, not orthographic survey material. Exact slopes, geographic orientation, invisible facades, roof drainage and structural systems are unknown.
- The assets use procedurally created mesh geometry and eight scalar PBR materials. No third-party models, logos, image textures, UV scans, PLATEAU data, or existing game assets are reused.
